title.id: Anatomi Portofolio Developer yang Membuat Rekruter Berhenti Scroll
title.en: The Anatomy of a Developer Portfolio That Makes Recruiters Stop Scrolling

excerpt.id: Struktur halaman, cara menulis studi kasus project, dan detail mikro yang membuat portofolio terasa profesional.
excerpt.en: Page structure, how to write project case studies, and the micro-details that make a portfolio feel professional.

content.id:
Portofolio adalah *landing page* pribadi — dan rekruter adalah user-nya. Mereka scroll cepat, keputusan dalam hitungan detik. Ini anatomi yang saya pelajari lewat banyak eksperimen.

## Aturan 5 Detik

Kunjungan pertama harus langsung menjawab tiga pertanyaan:

1. Siapa kamu? (nama + peran)
2. Apa keahlian intimu? (stack, bukan semua tools)
3. Apa langkah selanjutnya? (CTA jelas: lihat project / hubungi)

Hero yang baik itu pendek. Satu kalimat nilai jual, satu CTA. Selesai.

## Project: Tulis Studi Kasus, Bukan Katalog

Perbedaan terbesar antara portofolio biasa dengan yang memorable ada di *studi kasus*:

- **Masalah** apa yang diselesaikan?
- **Keputusan teknis** apa yang diambil, dan kenapa?
- **Hasil**nya apa? (angka lebih bagus: performa naik 40%, dsb.)

> Screenshot bagus menarik perhatian; cerita masalah-solusi-hasil yang membuat orang percaya kamu bisa memecahkan masalah mereka.

## Detail Mikro yang Sering Diremehkan

Hal-hal kecil ini yang membuat situs terasa "mahal":

1. Transisi halus tapi tidak berlebihan (150–300ms)
2. State hover/focus di **semua** elemen interaktif
3. Loading skeleton, bukan spinner kosong
4. Dark mode yang benar-benar dipoles
5. Meta tag OG rapi — share link ke WA/Slack tetap cantik

## Jangan Sempurnakan Sendirian

Tunjukkan draft ke 3–5 orang. Tanyakan satu hal: "setelah lihat 10 detik, kesan pertamamu apa?" Jawabannya hampir selalu membuka blind spot.

Portofolio terbaik bukan yang paling ramai animasi — tapi yang paling *jelas*. Semoga membantu!
content.en:
A portfolio is your personal *landing page* — and recruiters are its users. They scroll fast and decide in seconds. Here's the anatomy I learned through lots of experimentation.

## The 5-Second Rule

A first visit must instantly answer three questions:

1. Who are you? (name + role)
2. What are your core skills? (your stack, not every tool)
3. What's the next step? (a clear CTA: view work / contact)

A good hero is short. One value sentence, one CTA. Done.

## Projects: Write Case Studies, Not Catalogs

The biggest difference between ordinary portfolios and memorable ones is the *case study*:

- What **problem** did you solve?
- What **technical decisions** did you make, and why?
- What was the **result**? (numbers are better: 40% performance gain, etc.)

> Nice screenshots grab attention; problem-solution-result stories make people believe you can solve *their* problems.

## Micro-Details People Underrate

These small things make a site feel expensive:

1. Smooth but restrained transitions (150–300ms)
2. Hover/focus states on **every** interactive element
3. Loading skeletons instead of empty spinners
4. Dark mode that's actually polished
5. Clean OG meta tags — shared links still look great in WA/Slack

## Don't Polish Alone

Show your draft to 3–5 people. Ask one thing: "after seeing it for 10 seconds, what's your first impression?" The answer almost always exposes a blind spot.

The best portfolio isn't the one with the most animations — it's the *clearest* one. Hope this helps!
